title: Segal mapping-space descent for finite interval covers
statement:
Use small simplicial sets and the Kan model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], and simplicial spaces, outer representables $F(n)$, simplicial mapping spaces $\operatorname{Map}$ and the Reedy structure from [lem-coef-simplicial-space-reedy-cartesian]. Let $V$ be Reedy fibrant and assume that $V_m\to V_1\times_{V_0}\cdots\times_{V_0}V_1$ is a weak homotopy equivalence for every $m\geq2$.

For $n\geq0$ and a nonempty subset $S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n\}$, let $F(S)\subseteq F(n)$ consist of the monotone maps with image in $S$. Give $S$ its induced linear order. An interval cover of $F(S)$ means a subobject that is a union of full faces on consecutive intervals in that order and contains every vertex and every consecutive edge of $F(S)$. For $|S|=1$, the interval cover is $F(S)$ itself.

Let $\mathcal F$ be a finite family of nonempty subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n\}$, closed under nonempty intersections, and put $X=\bigcup_{S\in\mathcal F}F(S)$. Let $A\subseteq X$ be a simplicial subobject, discrete in the inner direction like $X$, such that $A\cap F(S)$ is an interval cover of $F(S)$ for every $S\in\mathcal F$. Then restriction is a trivial Kan fibration
$$\operatorname{Map}(X,V)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}(A,V).$$
The empty family is allowed, with $A=X=\varnothing$.

source.place: Rezk Lemma 10.1, printed p.23, and the finite face-cover gluing argument in Lemma 11.11, printed p.27. This is their finite intersection-closed face-family formulation, without equivalence-edge restrictions. Read online; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this Segal-space result.

proof.text: Write $M(B)=\operatorname{Map}(B,V)$, including $M(\varnothing)=*$. Every inclusion $B\subseteq C$ is a bidegree monomorphism and hence a Reedy cofibration by [lem-coef-simplicial-space-reedy-cartesian]. Apply that node to $V\to *$, a Reedy fibration by hypothesis: $M(C)\to M(B)$ is a Kan fibration. In particular every $M(B)$ is Kan by taking $B=\varnothing$. If $B,C$ are subobjects, their union is their pushout over $B\cap C$: degree by degree a map on the union is precisely two maps agreeing on the intersection. Products with $c\Delta^q$ preserve this union and intersection degree by degree. Thus, compatibly with all simplicial operators, $M(B\cup C)=M(B)\times_{M(B\cap C)}M(C)$. Also $F(S)\cap F(T)=F(S\cap T)$, with $F(\varnothing)=\varnothing$, since a monotone map has image in both sets exactly when it has image in their intersection.

source.place: Sections 2.3-2.5 and Lemma 11.11, printed p.27: mapping-space fibrations and the degreewise union/pullback calculation.

proof.text: We now prove a finite gluing assertion used twice below; its proof is steps 2-4, rather than an additional assumed result. Let $\mathcal H$ be any finite family of nonempty vertex subsets closed under nonempty intersections, put $Y=\bigcup_{T\in\mathcal H}F(T)$, and let $D\subseteq Y$. Assume only that $M(F(T))\to M(D\cap F(T))$ is a trivial Kan fibration for every $T\in\mathcal H$. The claim is that $M(Y)\to M(D)$ is a trivial Kan fibration. Induct strongly on $|\mathcal H|$, uniformly in $D$ and in the ambient simplex. The empty case is the identity of $*$. In the nonempty case choose an inclusion-maximal $S\in\mathcal H$ and set $\mathcal H'=\mathcal H\setminus\{S\}$, $Y'=\bigcup_{T\in\mathcal H'}F(T)$, $D'=D\cap Y'$, $E=D\cap F(S)$, and $K=Y'\cap F(S)$. The family $\mathcal H'$ is intersection-closed: an intersection of its members cannot equal $S$, since this would make each contain the maximal member $S$ and hence equal $S$. Define $\mathcal K$ to consist of the distinct nonempty sets $T\cap S$ with $T\in\mathcal H'$. These are proper subsets of $S$ by maximality, belong to $\mathcal H'$ by intersection-closure, and are closed under nonempty intersections, since $(T_1\cap S)\cap(T_2\cap S)=(T_1\cap T_2)\cap S$. Thus $|\mathcal K|\leq|\mathcal H'|<|\mathcal H|$, and $K=\bigcup_{U\in\mathcal K}F(U)$. Both induction applications are therefore legitimate. The local hypothesis for $Y',D'$ is the given hypothesis for $T\in\mathcal H'$. For $K,D\cap K$, it is the given hypothesis for $U\in\mathcal K$, because $F(U)\subseteq K$. Consequently $M(Y')\to M(D')$ and $M(K)\to M(D\cap K)$ are trivial Kan fibrations. No interval-cover hypothesis is used in this induction.

source.place: Lemma 10.1 proof, printed p. 23, for the finite face-union argument; the generalized strong-induction assertion and overlap family are proved explicitly here.

proof.text: Continue the induction step of step 2. Set $B=E\cup K\subseteq F(S)$. Then $E\cap K=D\cap K$, so step 1 identifies $M(B)\to M(E)$ with the pullback of the trivial Kan fibration $M(K)\to M(D\cap K)$ supplied by induction. Trivial Kan fibrations have the right lifting property against all boundary inclusions by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. A square against a pullback projection is a square against the original map with its fixed map to the pullback base; a filler for the latter, paired with that fixed map, is a filler for the former. Thus pullbacks of trivial Kan fibrations are trivial Kan fibrations. The composite $M(F(S))\to M(B)\to M(E)$ is the locally assumed trivial Kan fibration, while its second factor is trivial. Two-out-of-three in the model-category axioms of [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure], applied to the Kan model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], makes $M(F(S))\to M(B)$ a weak homotopy equivalence. It is a Kan fibration by step 1, hence a trivial Kan fibration. This argument applies even if $K$ is empty or disconnected.

source.place: Expanded pullback, boundary-lifting and two-out-of-three argument for the finite gluing step; the relevant model-category facts are cited by node, and no arbitrary-limit claim is used.

proof.text: Set $Z=D\cup Y'$. Because $D\subseteq Y=Y'\cup F(S)$, we have $Z=Y'\cup E$, $Z\cap F(S)=K\cup E=B$, and $D\cap Y'=D'$. Step 1 therefore identifies $M(Y)\to M(Z)$ with the pullback of the trivial Kan fibration $M(F(S))\to M(B)$ from step 3, and identifies $M(Z)\to M(D)$ with the pullback of the trivial Kan fibration $M(Y')\to M(D')$ from induction. The pullback argument in step 3 makes both maps trivial Kan fibrations. Their composite is one too: to solve a boundary-lifting square against a composite $P\to Q\to R$, first lift against $Q\to R$ with the boundary map to $Q$ obtained from the given boundary map to $P$, then lift against $P\to Q$. The characterization in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] concludes the induction and proves the finite gluing assertion of steps 2-4.

source.place: Expanded successive pullbacks completing the finite-gluing proof; analogous to the pullback pattern in Lemma 11.11, printed p. 27.

proof.text:
For a nonempty ordered vertex set $S$, define its spine $G(S)$ to be the union of its vertices and its consecutive edges. The increasing bijection $[m]\cong S$, $m=|S|-1$, identifies $F(S)$ with $F(m)$. A $q$-simplex of $M(F(m))$ is determined by evaluation at $1_{[m]}$: an element $v\in (V_m)_q$ gives the map whose value on $(\alpha:[k]\to[m],\beta:[r]\to[q])$ is $V(\alpha)(v|_\beta)$, and evaluation reverses this construction. Maps out of $G(S)$ are strings of $m$ maps out of $F(1)$ whose adjacent endpoints agree, by the union calculation in step 1. Hence restriction to $G(S)$ is precisely the displayed Segal map. By the standing hypothesis that $V_m\to V_1\times_{V_0}\cdots\times_{V_0}V_1$ is a weak homotopy equivalence for every $m\geq2$, this restriction is a weak homotopy equivalence for $m\geq2$, and it is an identity for $m=0,1$. It is a Kan fibration by step 1, so $M(F(S))\to M(G(S))$ is a trivial Kan fibration in every case.

Let $C\subseteq F(S)$ be a subobject that is a union of full faces on consecutive intervals in the induced order on $S$ and contains every vertex and consecutive edge of $F(S)$. Choose all nonempty intervals $I$ of $S$ for which $F(I)\subseteq C$; there are finitely many, their faces cover $C$, and their nonempty intersections are again such intervals. Since $I$ is consecutive in $S$, $G(S)\cap F(I)=G(I)$: a consecutive pair in $I$ is a consecutive pair in $S$, and conversely a spine simplex of $S$ lying in $I$ is a vertex or such an edge or its degeneracy. Apply the gluing assertion proved in steps 2-4 to this interval family with $Y=C$ and $D=G(S)$. Its local hypotheses are exactly the spine trivial fibrations just proved, including singleton intersections. It follows that $M(C)\to M(G(S))$ is a trivial Kan fibration. Its composite with $M(F(S))\to M(C)$ is the spine map, already a weak equivalence. Two-out-of-three from [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure] makes $M(F(S))\to M(C)$ a weak equivalence; step 1 makes it a Kan fibration. Thus it is a trivial Kan fibration. This proves the interval-cover case by an actual argument, without assuming it as another node.

source.place: Section 4.1 equation (4.1) and Lemma 10.1, printed p. 23, for the spine/cover comparison; the generalized interval-family gluing is expanded in steps 2–4.

proof.text: Apply the finite gluing assertion proved in steps 2-4 to $\mathcal H=\mathcal F$, $Y=X$, and $D=A$. For every $S\in\mathcal F$, the hypothesis on $A$ says exactly that $A\cap F(S)$ is an interval cover, so step 5 supplies its local trivial Kan fibration. The supplied intersection-closure is exactly the hypothesis needed in step 2 for every overlap, even when two original faces are not intervals of the ambient $[n]$. Therefore restriction $M(X)\to M(A)$ is a trivial Kan fibration. For the empty family, $A=X=\varnothing$ and the restriction is the identity of $*$, as in the induction base. For a singleton vertex family the local map is an identity; no nonempty-edge convention is needed.

source.place: Application of the finite-gluing argument to the interval-cover local comparisons from Lemma 10.1; the application is written explicitly here.
